headline: CMU Opens Its Computer Science Classroom
lede: Carnegie Mellon is placing full computer science lectures on YouTube, extending its classrooms beyond campus. The first release offers recordings across systems, robotics, software engineering, and AI; exercises, grading, and tutoring are still to come.

headline: Verification Becomes the AI Codebase’s Spine
lede: The Claude Code team describes a software process in which agents write most of the code, while independent checks supply the discipline. End-to-end tests lead; property tests, differential tests, incident records, and human review close the loop.
pullquote: When agents write the code, verification must become the system of record.

headline: A Visual Basic Time Capsule Reopens
lede: VisualBasic.World gathers programs published through Planet Source Code from 1997 to 2012. Business tools, games, controls, and experiments preserve an era when sharing a complete working program was part of the craft.

headline: Japan Turns Local Taxes Into A Marketplace
lede: Japan’s Hometown Tax lets residents redirect part of their future residence tax to municipalities of their choice. What began as regional redistribution became a nationwide catalog of food, travel, and municipal rewards.

headline: BugMeNot Closes Its Registration Escape Hatch
lede: BugMeNot, the long-running directory of shared logins, has shut down. Its disappearance closes one of the web’s scruffier answers to forced registration, leaving behind a farewell and an unexplained block of ciphertext.

headline: Nimony Builds A New Nim Foundation
lede: Nimony is a new compiler for Nim 3. Borrow checking, explicit nilability, sum types, native code generation, and WebAssembly support arrive in a pipeline designed to reduce old toolchain dependencies.

headline: A Trusted Script Pipeline Served Malware
lede: Optimizely customer JavaScript was compromised, sending malicious code through sites including Zoom, GitLab, the BBC, and CNN. The payload targeted cryptocurrency, payment data, cookies, screenshots, and iOS users. Audit third-party scripts; restrict their reach.

headline: macOS Narrows The Door To Protected Data
lede: Apple’s latest macOS controls let users grant some apps access to selected folders or applications instead of the whole disk. The quieter permission model acknowledges how much a broad exception can reveal: files, keystrokes, activity, and other apps.

headline: Why 3dfx Colors Looked Washed Out
lede: 3dfx’s color pipeline leaned toward linear light while its era’s displays and artwork assumed gamma encoding. With only five or six bits per channel, the technically principled path exposed banding, pale shadows, and a mismatch between mathematics and texture art.

headline: Chemistry Finds Its Shape In Reaction Networks
lede: Reaction network theory maps chemical species and reactions into vectors, subspaces, and compatibility classes. This geometric abstraction can reveal equilibria, oscillations, feedback, and pattern formation without fitting every molecular parameter.
